proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (bv_trace: 'Limit δ ↓ 0. Let δ_j := 1/(j + 4) ∈ (0, 1/4], δ_j ↓ 0; every point of Q₁ lies in Q_{δ_j} for all large j. ... By dominated convergence, ∫_{Q_{δ_j}} w div G → ∫_{Q₁} w div G'), stated for an arbitrary f integrable on Q₁ (dominated by |f| instead of M|w|) and along the filter δ → 0⁺, which contains the parent's sequence δ_j = 1/(j + 4) → 0⁺ as a special case.

Notation. Euclid k with Lebesgue measure volume; y_i is the i-th coordinate; Q₁ and Q_δ as in the statement (so Q₁ is the case a = 0, b = 1 and Q_δ the case a = δ, b = 1 − δ of the sets {z : a < z_i < b for all i}). 1_E denotes the indicator function of E.

1. Openness and measurability. For a, b ∈ ℝ, {z : a < z_i < b for all i} = ⋂_{i ∈ Fin k} ({z : a < z_i} ∩ {z : z_i < b}). Each coordinate map z ↦ z_i is continuous (PiLp.continuous_apply), so each {z : a < z_i} and {z : z_i < b} is open, and a finite intersection of open sets is open (isOpen_iInter_of_finite). Hence Q₁ and every Q_δ are open, in particular Borel measurable.

2. Inclusion. If δ ≥ 0 then Q_δ ⊆ Q₁: from δ < z_i < 1 − δ we get 0 ≤ δ < z_i and z_i < 1 − δ ≤ 1.

3. Reduction to a fixed measure. Let δ > 0; the set (0, ∞) of such δ belongs to 𝓝[>] 0. Since Q_δ is measurable and Q_δ ⊆ Q₁ (steps 1–2), ∫_{Q₁} 1_{Q_δ} f = ∫_{Q₁ ∩ Q_δ} f = ∫_{Q_δ} f (setIntegral_indicator and Q₁ ∩ Q_δ = Q_δ). So the functions δ ↦ ∫_{Q₁} 1_{Q_δ} f and δ ↦ ∫_{Q_δ} f agree eventually along 𝓝[>] 0, and it suffices (Tendsto.congr') to prove ∫_{Q₁} 1_{Q_δ} f → ∫_{Q₁} f as δ → 0⁺.

4. Dominated convergence. Apply the dominated convergence theorem for the countably generated filter 𝓝[>] 0 (tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence) to the measure volume⌞Q₁, the functions F_δ := 1_{Q_δ} f, the limit f and the bound |f|:
 (a) every F_δ is a.e.-strongly measurable for volume⌞Q₁, because f is (it is integrable on Q₁) and Q_δ is measurable (step 1);
 (b) |F_δ(y)| ≤ |f(y)| for every y and δ (norm of an indicator);
 (c) |f| is integrable on Q₁ because f is;
 (d) for volume⌞Q₁-a.e. y — namely for every y ∈ Q₁, which suffices because Q₁ is measurable (ae_restrict_iff') — F_δ(y) → f(y) as δ → 0⁺. Indeed, fix y ∈ Q₁ and i ∈ Fin k. Since 0 < y_i and 0 < 1 − y_i, every δ in a neighbourhood of 0 satisfies δ < y_i and δ < 1 − y_i, i.e. δ < y_i < 1 − δ; restricting to 𝓝[>] 0 ≤ 𝓝 0 this holds eventually along 𝓝[>] 0. Fin k is finite, so these finitely many eventualities hold simultaneously (Filter.eventually_all): eventually along 𝓝[>] 0, y ∈ Q_δ, and then F_δ(y) = f(y). So δ ↦ F_δ(y) is eventually equal to the constant f(y), hence converges to f(y).
 Dominated convergence gives ∫_{Q₁} F_δ → ∫_{Q₁} f as δ → 0⁺, and by step 3, ∫_{Q_δ} f → ∫_{Q₁} f as δ → 0⁺. ∎
key_steps: Each set {z : a < z_i < b ∀ i} is a finite intersection of open coordinate half-spaces, so Q₁ and all Q_δ are open and measurable.
For δ ≥ 0, Q_δ ⊆ Q₁, so for δ > 0, ∫_{Q_δ} f = ∫_{Q₁} 1_{Q_δ} f.
Every y ∈ Q₁ lies in Q_δ for all sufficiently small δ > 0 (finitely many coordinates; Filter.eventually_all), so 1_{Q_δ} f → f pointwise on Q₁.
Dominated convergence along the countably generated filter 𝓝[>] 0 with bound |f| (integrable on Q₁) gives ∫_{Q_δ} f → ∫_{Q₁} f.
